feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. The controller is the iteration 6 controller unchanged, because iteration 6 (70.83) is the best score and the only gain change (iteration 1) was confounded and scored lower. The evidence supports the span test. Iteration 6 showed one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error 0.0641 and 0.0669 m and low steering oscillation (0.133 to 0.148), so the robot drifts rather than jitters. Several levers are now closed: y 0.07 m did not remove the loss (iteration 3), body_length 0.12 m lowered the score (iteration 5), mass is at its 0.4 kg floor (iteration 6 beat iteration 4), and the 8 mm footprint lowered the score (iteration 7, 67.75). Read the next race by these branches. If line losses fall below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom and the score exceeds 70.83, keep the ±0.04 m span. If line losses stay at 1.0 with max_error still at or above 0.06 m and progress flat, span is not the limit, and the next test is wheel_track 0.14 m to damp turn rate. If the centre reads near 1 on every step and the oval gets worse, the 0.02 m spacing is saturating the signal, so return to ±0.03 m.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_size at 0.012 m and mass at 0.4 kg, and test the outer sensors at x = ±0.04 m with 0.02 m spacing, as in this race. Iteration 7 (8 mm) fell to 67.75, and iteration 6 (12 mm, ±0.03 m) reached 70.83, so 12 mm is the footprint to keep while span is tested.

If line_loss_events stay at 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom and progress is unchanged, return the span to ±0.03 m and try wheel_track 0.14 m with the other fields as in iteration 6. Iteration 1 (narrow 0.10 m track with higher gain) gave no benefit from faster turning, so this is a damping test, not a speed gain.
If the centre sensor reads near 1 on the middle steps and the oval score drops, the 0.02 m spacing is blurring small errors. Return to ±0.03 m spacing, which gave the iteration 6 best score.
